honest_limitations: SINGLE binary system (toluene+2-propanol); one chemistry class (aromatic + secondary alcohol). n_systems = 1 -> NOT promotable; a cross-pair d12 model needs many rights-clean binaries.

The NON-associating contrast case (e.g. toluene+n-heptane, benzene+cyclohexane) where Kendall-Monroe is expected to VALIDATE was NOT tested -- no rights-clean CC-BY table was fetchable this run (candidates were ACS/Springer paywalled). Claim is scoped to the associating case only.

Grunberg-Nissan d12 is FIT to interior points, so its low residual is an interpolation quality, not an a-priori prediction. It is reported to size the value of one measured datum, not as autonomous science.

Densities were tabulated only at 298.15 K, so the full Eyring excess Gibbs activation energy (needs molar volumes at all T) is reported by sign only via the log-viscosity excess, not as an absolute kJ/mol curve.

marine_relevance: Marine epoxy thinners are multi-solvent blends (aromatic + ketone + alcohol). This result says a formulator CANNOT hit an airless-spray viscosity target for an alcohol-containing blend from pure-component data alone -- the blend runs ~10-25% thinner than log-linear -- and must anchor at least one measured mid-composition viscosity per associating pair. That is a concrete, testable formulation rule.
new_axis_justification: grep of all 66 signed receipts + prior AUDIT axes for blend|mixing rule|Kendall|Grunberg|Refutas found ZERO hits: every prior viscosity artifact is a PURE-component Arrhenius fit or a CONTEXT_ONLY-quarantined polyverse MELT model. Component->mixture viscosity is the untouched, decision-relevant piece for a thinner blend.
non_circularity: Kendall-Monroe consumes ONLY the measured pure toluene and pure 2-propanol viscosity (x1=0, x1=1 rows) at each temperature. The 9 interior blend viscosities are the validation target and are NEVER an input to the zero-parameter prediction.

target_capability: Predict the dynamic viscosity of a formulated marine-coating solvent BLEND (thinner) from its pure-component viscosities and composition -- the application-rheology property that sets the airless-spray window, sag resistance and achievable film build. This is the blend-level counterpart to the module's existing pure-solvent Arrhenius fixture.
theory: Arrhenius (1887) / Kendall-Monroe (1917) zero-parameter log-linear mole-fraction mixing: ln eta_mix = sum_i x_i ln eta_i. Grunberg & Nissan (1949) one-parameter interaction extension: + x1 x2 d12. The excess ln-viscosity x1 x2 d12 equals the Eyring excess Gibbs energy of activation of viscous flow divided by RT (sign convention: negative for H-bond-disrupting aromatic+alcohol blends).
verdict: BLEND_VISCOSITY_MIXING_RULE_ESTABLISHED :: KENDALL_MONROE_ZERO_PARAM_REFUTED_ON_MAGNITUDE (global MAPE 33.9%, all 45 blend points over-predict across all 5 T -> systematic negative deviation for this associating aromatic+alcohol marine thinner) :: RANK_ORDER_VALIDATED (Spearman +1.0 every T) :: GRUNBERG_NISSAN_ONE_PARAM_VALIDATED (residual MAPE 3.0%, d12=-1.56). TRUSTWORTHY OUTPUT = one measured interaction datum (d12) per associating pair; pure-component-only blend prediction OVER-predicts spray/sag viscosity and is NOT trustworthy for alcohol-containing thinners. For the module: blend viscosity needs >=1 measured mid-composition point per associating pair, or a group-contribution d12 (future work, data-blocked).
